items.text: First gathering of Quarter 2 — the container re-held slowly after the break
“Take ninety seconds: one sentence about the Examen, or about how the break treated your practice, or anything that has shifted.”
“Thinned out over the break is a completely normal answer — the practice picks up where you are.”
A parent starts the round — pass-anytime holds
Week 6 still sitting heavy? “The team is here. Find one of us before you leave tonight.”
One short verse, three steps: Word → Hearing → Faith — the order matters
Not trying harder, not emotional experience — faith is a fruit of a particular practice
How much of our “Bible time” is actually hearing, and how much is reading without hearing?
Hearing is a skill — skills develop with practice
The practice: PROAPT — Pray, Read, Observe, Apply, Pray again, Tell (Truro Church, 1980s)

panel.label: ROMANS 10:17
lines: “So faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of Christ.”

items.text: Pray — “Holy Spirit, you are welcome here. Speak. We are listening.”
Read — slowly, to receive it; don’t analyze yet
Observe — two layers, in order: first the data (who, what, when, where — straight off the page), then the interpretation — what stands out or surprises you in it
Apply — “What does this passage mean FOR YOU, TODAY, in your specific life?” — logos becomes rhema
Pray again — tell God what you heard, what you are willing to do, what you’re struggling to be willing to do
Tell — the most-often-skipped step; hearing spoken aloud has a different staying power

slides.title: Bridge to the Clusters — Pair Structure

items.text: Pair up in your family cluster — parent with teen, from your own family, by default
One Reader, one Listener — Reader leads the six steps; after twelve minutes, switch
“Pairing up with your own parent or your own teen is not the consolation-prize version — it is the design working.”
Your Cluster Companion settles the pairs and completes any odd numbers
Small room (about ten or fewer)? Stay as one circle and pair up in place
First pass (12 min) — Reader leads PROAPT; Listener works alongside without interrupting
Reader’s Tell at the end goes to the Listener — one sentence
Switch roles — new passage or stay with Mark 1
Second pass (12 min) — same structure, roles reversed
Stuck on Observe? “What’s one specific word or phrase that caught your attention?”
“Slow down. The Spirit isn’t in a hurry.” — and if you finish early, get reps with another passage

slides.title: Tell Step — Sharing in the Cluster

items.text: Back in the family cluster — each of us tells ONE specific thing we heard tonight
“Specific. One sentence. We listen to receive, like Week 3.”
A parent opens the round — arranged beforehand, never a cold call on a teen; pass-anytime holds
Receive without preaching — “We hear that.” “Thank you for naming that.”
“What we heard tonight is not just for us — it is given to us to walk out.”
One word each — not what you heard (that’s yours), but what tonight’s practice was like; a parent begins
Daily PROAPT — one passage per day, every day, for the next week — five to ten minutes
The journal Week 7 pages have a daily PROAPT template
Passage paths on the handout — the Gospel of Mark, the Sermon on the Mount, or Romans 8
Commit aloud to a specific time of day — “Morning before school” / “Right after dinner”
“The chain only works if we work it.”
